question: Can a digit-matrix grid place a trained-depth ceiling, or is its accuracy indistinguishable from option guessing and one-component shortcut solving?

rows.G1_chance_floor: content-free floor per level: best constant option index on the dispatched item set, reported next to the nominal 1/8
rows.G2_signal: signal at level L iff correct_L >= 5/15 AND Wilson95 lower bound > G1 floor AND exact two-sided binomial p vs 1/8 < 0.05; all three must hold
rows.G3_d_hat: d_hat over the tested levels per evaluation/frozen/rule.json trained_depth (mastery 0.80, greatest L with ACC >= 0.80 for every level <= L); not_evaluable when a level delivers nothing
rows.G4_parse_integrity: count of judged option indices outside 0..7 (must be 0) and count of records whose judged letter also appears earlier in the completion (last-letter-wins ambiguity)
rows.G5_delivery_census: counts per DELIVERY_STATES per level; n is the dispatched count, never the answered count
rows.G6_determinism: the two byte-identical re-dispatches must reproduce the judged value of their first dispatch; divergence flags dup_pair_diverges
rows.G7_option_histogram: diagnostic only, no tier input: the model's judged option-index histogram against the item key histogram
rows.G8_rate_gate: pre-dispatch measured completion-token rate selects the plan: >= 20.0 tok/s full plan, >= 5.0 tok/s reduced plan n=8, below that no dispatch
